rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Friday call preceded the sermon; ‘Uthmān added a second call as Madīnah grew, and the community adopted it without objection.
rows.anchor: The caliph ‘Uthm ān (rta) added one more call when in his times the population of Madīnah increased

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb translated ‘hasten’ primarily means acting eagerly and alertly, not simply running; it can describe a slave hastening to answer a master's call.
rows.anchor: primarily used to do something with fervour and enthusiasm while being vigilant

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the Friday call, believers should hasten to God's remembrance and leave trading aside.
rows.anchor: people should hasten to God’s remembrance and leave aside trading activities

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's remembrance includes both prayer and sermon; the sermon replaces two of the four noon rak‘ats and covers Muslims' needs, not only prescribed supplications.
rows.anchor: There is no reason to confine this remembrance to some specific supplications.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word for selling primarily means sale but is commonly used for both selling and purchasing.
rows.anchor: primarily means “to sell.” However, in its general usage, it is used for both sale and purchase

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sale is singled out because the incident that tested the Muslims involved trading; leaving sale therefore implies leaving purchase too, and the command covers worldly activity generally.
rows.anchor: incident which became a trial for the Muslims and on which they were warned related to trading and sale and purchase

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Leaving business for God may look like financial loss, but earns lasting reward and may even be compensated in this life because sustenance is God's; assess gain and loss with the Hereafter in view.
rows.anchor: Livelihood and sustenance are all in the hands of God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The appeal to those who would understand urges them to judge benefit and loss beyond this world's limited lifespan, though the Hereafter is understood only by those who truly seek to understand it.
rows.anchor: the limited life-span of theirs in this world; they should also keep in mind the Hereafter

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Muslims cannot accept the brief Friday restriction for God's pleasure, it shows deficient faith; Jews faced Sabbath restrictions all day, while Muslims are restricted only from the call through prayer and are otherwise free.
rows.anchor: if, for the pleasure of God, they are not able to abide by this restriction which is only till the Friday prayer

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Livelihood seeking is permitted, but those seeking the next world's benefit must remember God at every step; this protects them from Satan and from losing their moral bearings to worldly temptation.
rows.anchor: This remembrance which will save them from the deceptions and trials of Satan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Narratives report that a trade caravan arrived during the Friday sermon, drums announced it, and some people left the Prophet while he preached.
rows.anchor: It is evident from some narratives 12 that a trade caravan entered Madīnah right at the time of the Friday sermon.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Caravans were eagerly awaited because they carried important goods; people competed to buy from them and sell their own goods.
rows.anchor: Such caravans had a lot of importance in those days.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who left were insufficiently grounded in Islamic teaching and the sermon’s importance; they apparently thought only the prayer mattered and expected to return before it began.
rows.anchor: they thought that it was only the prayer that was important

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their error occasioned divine guidance for the community on Friday, its prayer, and the Prophet's status, matters not previously addressed in this way.
rows.anchor: their mistake afforded the opportunity of divine guidance being revealed for the ummah regarding Friday

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the address is general, only a few uncouth individuals made this error; the Qur'an avoids naming wrongdoers so everyone can learn without humiliating anyone.
rows.anchor: The general style of the Qur’ ān is that it does not rebuke people

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording that the Prophet was left standing stresses the incident's gravity: he himself was delivering the sermon, making the departure a serious disrespect.
rows.anchor: the sermon was being delivered by the Prophet (sws) himself

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Jews showed the same disregard toward Moses, and God consequently distorted their hearts, as Sūrah al-Ṣaff says.
rows.anchor: The Jews had adopted precisely the same attitude with Moses (sws).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's reward surpasses worldly amusement and trade: accepting even great worldly loss for God and His Prophet brings an eternal kingdom, while worldly riches gained by displeasing them are fleeting.
rows.anchor: they will attain an eternal kingdom in lieu of the meagre possessions they have

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the best provider, supplying pure and wholesome sustenance from sources a person could not imagine.
rows.anchor: provides sustenance from places a person cannot even imagine

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though the Qur'an does not mention Friday prayer elsewhere, the Prophet instituted it in Madīnah and taught its rites; Qur'anic admonition treats his directives as God's, so rejecting them after their attribution to him is rejecting God's directives.
rows.anchor: once this ascription is verified, then rejecting them is like rejecting the directives of God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sermon is an essential part of Friday prayer, replacing two rak‘ats and divided into two parts; both sermon and prayer are remembrance of God, though the imam faces the congregation in the sermon.
rows.anchor: The Friday sermon is an important constituent of the Friday prayer.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Modern practice wrongly reduces the real sermon to conventional supplications while long, irrelevant pre-sermon speeches tire listeners; imams should give brief, wise reminders and people should attend on time.
rows.anchor: The way to do this is that the imāms, instead of indulging in long speeches should spend time in reminding people of things that constitute the real sermon.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preferred Friday routine is to prepare for prayer beforehand and leave activities that could interfere until afterward, unless there is a compelling need; grooming and washing also suit Friday, and trade should begin after prayer.
rows.anchor: the time before the Friday prayer should be spent in its preparation

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier scholars followed this post-prayer routine, which remains appreciated in religious circles conscious of Islamic customs.
rows.anchor: scholars of the past have conformed to this very routine

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discussion has limited itself to what can be deduced directly from the Qur'an about Friday prayer and leaves related jurisprudential issues untreated.
rows.anchor: I have confined myself in the discussion above to what can be deduced directly from the Qur’ān regarding the Friday prayer.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūrah Nūḥ follows al-Ma‘ārij, where the Prophet was urged to endure demands to hasten punishment; Noah's story illustrates the long patience a messenger must exercise.
rows.anchor: In Sūrah al-Ma‘ ārij, the previous sūrah, readers have seen that the Prophet (sws) was urged to exercise patience

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account of Noah's preaching, prolonged waiting, patience, and his people's eventual punishment shows the Prophet and his people the arduous delays on a messenger's path.
rows.anchor: the tale of Prophet Noah’s phases of preaching, his protracted period of waiting and exercising patience during it

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite haste, scorn, and allegations, God grants people long respite but ultimately seizes them so completely that none can rescue them.
rows.anchor: the Almighty does give a long respite to people; however, He finally seizes them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's sequence is clear and follows Noah's preaching mission, with some verses inserted on the spot; their nature will be explained in the exegesis.
rows.anchor: Some verses have come in between this discourse as on the spot insertions ( taḍmīn).
